newsitem.title: USA: Sun Television to close nine stores.
newsitem.headline: Sun Television to close nine stores.

text.p: Sun Television and Appliances Inc. said Tuesday it plans to withdraw from New York State and the Dayton and Springfield, Ohio, markets by March 1 and will post a fourth-quarter charge from closing nine stores.
For the fiscal year to date, the nine stores generated sales of $74 million, about 15 percent of Sun's consolidated sales, and recorded an operating loss of $2 million.
Columbus, Ohio-based Sun, whose fiscal year ends March 1, did not specify the size of the expected charge.

"Our third-quarter results, coupled with the continuing sales and margin difficulties plaguing the consumer electronics and home office industry, clearly indicate the need for a more aggressive and decisive plan of action to return the company to profitability," Sun President and Chief Executive James Copitzky said in a statement.

"Although we are disappointed that it is necessary to exit these markets ... it is critical that we take these steps to secure the long-term health of the company. While our exit from these markets will have an immediate positive impact on cash flow, we also expect longer-term benefits as we identify corporate expense reductions as a result of the closings."
Copitzy said the company expects its operating environment in the foreseeable future to remain intensely competitive.
Sun is closing five stores in New York State, three in the Dayton area and one in Springfield, Ohio.
Sun's stock was down 31.25 cents at $2.50 in morning trading on the Nasdaq system.
